items.title: Mavericks Win West Group A In NBA Cup
items.summary: The Mavericks are the first team to officially advance in this year’s NBA Cup tournament, clinching West Group A when Phoenix lost at Houston Wednesday night, writes Eddie Sefko of NBA.com. Dallas is 3-0 in the group with wins over Houston, Utah and Denver and a +36 point differential. The Nuggets could potentially catch them at 3-1, but the Mavs own the tiebreaker based on a 120-101 victory at Denver Tuesday night. Quarterfinal action in the tournament will take place December 4 and 5, with the semifinals set for December 8 and 9. The Mavericks seemed like a long shot to advance through a challenging group when Cup play began, but Sefko states that each victory sparked more excitement about the chance to be involved in high-stakes elimination games early in the season. “I’m into it. items.title: Jaylen Brown To Undergo Imaging After Leaving Game With Hamstring Tightness
items.summary: Sixers forward Jaylen Brown was removed from Wednesday’s game against Miami after experiencing tightness in his left hamstring, according to Kris Rhim of ESPN. Coach Nick Nurse said medical imaging will take place, and an update on Brown’s condition will be issued on Thursday (Twitter link). Brown exited late in the second quarter after hitting a step-back jumper, Rhim details. He shook his head and grabbed at the hamstring, then signaled to the bench that he needed to be replaced. He finished with six points, one rebound and one assist in 17 minutes as Philadelphia posted a 111-104 victory in the NBA Cup contest. Rhim notes that Brown’s hamstring issues began in a November 16 game against Brooklyn. He tied a season high with 31 points, but had to leave with a hamstring strain and sat out the next two contests against Orlando and Milwaukee. He returned on Monday with 20 points against…

items.summary: Caleb Martin’s first full season with the Mavericks was disappointing, but he has emerged as a valuable three-and-D wing this year, writes Eddie Sefko of NBA.com. After being limited to 58 games last season by back, heel and ankle injuries, along with an extended illness, Martin is back to full health and looks more like the player he was earlier in his career. “He’s just comfortable,” P.J. Washington said. “Last year, he was dealing with injuries. This year, he’s more back to himself, finding a rhythm. We love him being out there doing whatever he wants on the defensive end. Obviously, he’s guarding the best guards every night. We need his energy and he creates a lot of fast breaks.” Martin, who has become the on-court leader of an improved Dallas defense, tied a career high with five steals in Tuesday’s win at Denver. items.title: Tyrese Haliburton Nears Return From Hamstring Injury
items.summary: Tyrese Haliburton was a full participant in the Pacers’ practice on Wednesday, but a decision hasn’t been made on when he’ll be ready for game action, writes Tony East of Circle City Spin. The star guard, who hasn’t played since straining his left hamstring in an October 26 game, recently posted on social media that he wants to resume playing by the end of the month. Indiana’s only remaining November games are Friday against Philadelphia and Saturday at Chicago, so it’s not clear if he’ll be able to meet that goal. Haliburton, who also practiced on Tuesday with the G League’s Noblesville Boom, believes the sessions are the final step toward being cleared to play, but added that the Pacers’ medical staff is being cautious. “I think, being completely honest, the organization is doing as best they can protecting me from myself, you know,” he told reporters after today’s practice.…

items.title: NBA Announces Plans For European Arena Development, Renovations
items.summary: The NBA has announced plans for an initiative that would target approximately $11 billion in funding toward the development and renovation of basketball arenas – and the sports and entertainment districts around them – across Europe, according to a league press release. It’s part of the league’s plan — in partnership with FIBA — to launch NBA Europe next year.
